passage:
By second year, Yusuf was my weather. If his messages were cheerful, I was fine; if they were short, I spent the afternoon rereading them. I asked him which elective to pick, what to wear, even whether to go home for Diwali. I'd quit the dance club because he wasn't there, and weekends without him felt hollow.

"Reena, are you seriously waiting for him to text first again?" my roommate said one Saturday.

I sat there, ashamed, then went to dance practice out of spite. Halfway through a step I caught myself laughing with people who didn't know or care what Yusuf thought. I could still be someone without him in the room. That surprised me, and it made choosing him feel different, lighter.

qa.q: Which questions did Reena ask Yusuf to decide for her?
qa.a: Reena asked him which elective to pick, what to wear, and whether to go home for Diwali.

qa.q: How did Reena feel on weekends without Yusuf, and what shows it?
qa.a: Reena felt lost and empty, since she says the weekends felt hollow and she quit the dance club because he was not there.

qa.q: What step helped Reena, and why might it work?
qa.a: Going back to dance practice helped, because having Reena's own friends and interests means being with Yusuf becomes a choice, not a need.

qa.q: How might Yusuf have felt being the source of all of Reena's moods?
qa.a: He may have felt weighed down, unable to have a short or bad day without worrying it would upset Reena.

grounding: Shows leaning on a partner for mood and decisions, then rebuilding one's own friends and activities so love becomes a choice.

passage:
Dear Jatin,
I've been thinking since our fight on Sunday, and I want to say something I couldn't say out loud.
I've made you my everything, and that isn't fair to you. When you're busy, my whole day goes grey. I haven't decided a single thing this semester without asking you first, not even which elective to take. I stopped going to my Wednesday dance class because it clashed with your free evening. When you said you wanted a weekend with your school friends, I sulked as if you were leaving me.
That's not you doing anything wrong. That's me handing you my whole happiness and then being angry when you can't hold it.
So I'm changing things. I've rejoined dance. I'm going home to Indore for my sister's birthday on my own. I chose the elective myself, the one I actually like.
I want to love you because I choose you, not because I can't stand up without you.
Jyoti

qa.q: Which class did Jyoti stop going to?
qa.a: The Wednesday dance class, because it clashed with Jatin's free evening.

qa.q: How did Jyoti feel when Jatin wanted a weekend with school friends?
qa.a: Jyoti felt abandoned and sulked, as if being left.

qa.q: What changes is Jyoti making, and why do they help?
qa.a: Rejoining dance, visiting home alone and choosing the elective, so life has its own anchors beyond Jatin.

qa.q: How might Jatin feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Likely relieved and touched, freed from carrying Jyoti's whole happiness.

grounding: A letter from a young person who has leaned on a partner for mood and decisions, choosing to rebuild their own friends and goals.

passage: So, Meghna, you want to know why I'm at the gym at seven? It's a long story, but I'm Kalyani and you're my oldest friend, so sit. When Pankaj left for his internship in Hyderabad in May, I fell apart. Not heartbreak; nothing happened between us. I just realised I didn't know what to do with myself. For a year he'd chosen our films, our food, even whether I should cut my hair. When he didn't reply for four hours, my whole mood dropped. On day three I cried because I couldn't decide what to have for dinner. That's when I thought: this isn't love, this is leaning so hard I've forgotten how to stand. So I started small. Joined the gym. Called you. Picked up the sketching I'd dropped in second year. When Pankaj came back, I told him all of it. He said, 'You seem more you.' I think that's the best thing he's ever said.

qa.q: Where did Pankaj go for his internship?
What did Kalyani feel on day three of Pankaj's internship?
qa.a: Kalyani felt lost and helpless, crying over not being able to decide what to have for dinner.

qa.q: What small steps helped Kalyani stop depending so heavily on Pankaj?
qa.a: Joining the gym, calling Meghna, and picking up sketching again.

qa.q: How does Pankaj see Kalyani when he returns?
qa.a: He says Kalyani seems 'more you', noticing a fuller, more independent self.

grounding: A spoken account of a young person who realises they depend on a partner for mood and decisions and rebuilds their own interests and friendships.
